correctness.rationale: Assessed the corrected RESULT.md under /workspace/repairs/5. The six masks are exactly the monic odd quintics with neither x+1 nor x²+x+1 as a factor; every reducible quintic has a factor of degree at most two, and 31 is prime, so the irreducible quintics are primitive. The parity-check columns are all distinct nonzero five-bit vectors, giving dimension 26 and distance 3 (any two distinct columns sum to a third). The bundled finite recurrences count internal windows at append and the remaining b−1 cyclic windows at closure; the second uses character orthogonality instead of retaining syndrome states. Independent enumeration used neither recurrence: evaluate all 2²⁶ binary polynomial multiples of each degree-five p with degree at most 30, exactly the words satisfying c(α)=0, and count nonzero windows by popcount of the OR of b consecutive cyclic rotations. All 576 coefficients, reciprocal pairs, and nine displayed coefficient pairs matched. Replay: /workspace/branches/05-direct-multiples.py; arrays: /workspace/branches/05-direct-multiples-output.json. Reversal sends a polynomial to x³⁰c(x⁻¹) and takes C_p to the code of the reciprocal polynomial without altering the cyclic window count. The frozen first-moment explanation used independence of the window columns, which is not sufficient to prove uniformity of the projection from the kernel. The repaired proof uses the complementary columns: at least 27 distinct nonzero columns cannot lie in a proper subspace, so every window pattern has 2^(26−b) completions. Summing over the 31 window positions proves the invariant for all eighteen arrays. The repair changes no coefficients, parameter ranges or classification.

value.rationale: Primitive cyclic order is intrinsic to how these codes are used in a cyclic read metric, while their ordinary weight enumerators are invariant under permutation. Length 31 is a natural first degree at which several reciprocal classes of primitive binary generators are available: degrees 3 and 4 have two primitive polynomials each forming one reciprocal pair, and degree 2 has only one. The complete spectra show that reversal accounts for all equalities at each tested read width and precisely quantify how distinct orderings with identical ordinary Hamming and dual b-symbol enumerators separate. Those coefficients are useful as exact benchmarks for order-sensitive cyclic metrics; no claim is made for arbitrary interleavers, longer lengths, or all b.
